note: Approved, deployed surfaces only. The full list lives in registry-master.json.

surfaces.name: SPLIT
surfaces.blurb: Figure-ground reversal type generator. Two tones only, always exact opposites — grid and pinwheel modes, up to 48 blades per glyph. The reversal is conserved: nothing lost or added in the exchange.

surfaces.name: Sortition Congress
surfaces.blurb: A legislature chosen by lot instead of election. A working model of government by random sample.

surfaces.name: CIRCLEFORNIA
surfaces.blurb: Measures any point on Earth against California. A california equivalent finder — the state as a unit of comparison.

surfaces.name: SOMESET GENERATOR
surfaces.blurb: A sunset that never settles. Geometry fixed, colour continuous — mostly almost-plausible, sometimes not. Press set to freeze one mid-transition, rise to let it go.

surfaces.name: BZ
surfaces.blurb: A chemical clock rendered as a field: bromate oxidation held far enough from equilibrium that it oscillates instead of settling. Three coupled species on a torus, each cell reacting against the mean of its neighbours — reaction against diffusion. The spiral cores are phase singularities, points where the oscillation has no defined phase and the medium must wind around them.

surfaces.name: POLYRHYTHMIC TIME CLOCK
surfaces.blurb: A clock that rings the time. Thirteen nested intervals — hour, half hour, minute, second — each striking on its own real boundary, so the polyrhythm is the clock's own arithmetic rather than something invented for it. Nine musical rings divide the bar against them at whatever tempo you set. Everything lands together on the minute; the whole field lands on the hour.

surfaces.name: KELP
surfaces.blurb: Seven strands of kelp hanging in a current, each a spring chain with its own sway period. A strand speaks only at the moment it finishes a sway and reverses — the turn is the beat, so the rhythm belongs to the water rather than to a grid laid over it. Each strand is tuned to its own scale and its own octave, low at the left and high at the right, and rings a cascade up or down that scale when it turns. Four beds retune the whole forest at once; density sets how hard a sway has to be before it counts as a strike.

surfaces.name: SEMANTIC VOYAGE
surfaces.blurb: Twenty thousand English words placed by meaning — real GloVe vectors projected into three dimensions, so that neighbours in the language stay neighbours in the room. You travel only by similarity: each word offers the handful nearest it, and reaching anywhere means finding a chain of small resemblances. Frequency works as stellar magnitude, so common words carry across the whole field and rare ones resolve only when you are close.

surfaces.name: ROOM
surfaces.blurb: After Alvin Lucier, who recorded his voice in a room and played the recording back into the room until the resonance had eaten the words. Here the room is a thesaurus and the speech is a sentence. Each scroll plays the text back one more time: every word is answered by one adjacent in meaning, held to the same syllable count, so the pulse is untouched while the sense drains out of it. Function words are the walls and never move, and a word repeated is always answered alike — repetition is what reinforces. Four rooms reflect differently, by sense, by association, by sound. There is no way back up the tape.
